plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.

interactionPlan.concept: In UV spectroscopy, the wavelength of maximum absorbance (λ_max) characterizes a conjugated system, while longer wavelengths show minimal absorption.

demo_steps.title: UV Absorption Spectrum
demo_steps.narration: This spectrum plots how strongly 1,3-butadiene absorbs ultraviolet light across different wavelengths.

demo_steps.title: Finding λ_max
demo_steps.narration: Use the slider to trace the curve. The absorbance reaches its absolute maximum at 217 nm, identifying this as the compound's λ_max.

demo_steps.title: The Absorption Peak
demo_steps.narration: The vast majority of the UV absorption occurs in a narrow, steep band between 200 and 250 nm.

demo_steps.title: The Transparent Tail
demo_steps.narration: Beyond 250 nm, the absorbance drops to near zero, indicating that the molecule is essentially transparent to longer UV wavelengths.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The defining feature of a UV spectrum is λ_max, the single wavelength where the molecule absorbs light most intensely, surrounded by regions of near-total transparency.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Line plot with y=0 at the bottom. Use a faint pink gradient for the background to match the textbook style. The trace is a smooth, continuous magenta line. The arrows on the axis labels should be prominent magenta arrows. When a region is highlighted via the toggle, use a semi-transparent shaded box or fill under the curve to emphasize that specific span of wavelengths, dimming the non-highlighted portion slightly. Ensure the slider dot correctly maps to the curve's y-value for any given x.

authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a peak at (217, 0.85) where lambda max equals 217 nanometers. The x-axis and y-axis represent wavelength and absorbance, respectively.

discrepancies: The static "λ_max = 217 nm" label collides with the interactive dot's tooltip box at the default position.
The magenta arrows indicating axis directions are drawn as long lines extending to the ends of the axes, whereas in the source they are shorter arrows placed adjacent to the text.
The top and right borders of the plot area are missing, whereas the source figure encloses the pink background with a solid black frame.
The x-axis tick marks point outwards (down) in the generated figure, but inwards (up) in the source.
evaluation.notes: The mathematical model and curve shape are highly accurate and the interactivity adds great pedagogical value, but label placement issues cause a noticeable collision at the peak.
action_items: Adjust the offsets for the live scrubber tooltip box or the static 'λ_max = 217 nm' label so they do not collide when the scrubber is at the peak (the default state).

Modify the magenta axis arrows to match the source: place them parallel to or immediately following the text as short arrows, rather than drawing them as long collinear segments extending to the edges.
Draw a black stroke around the top and right edges of the chartArea to match the boxed appearance of the source figure.
